title: Running the cell-window machine
statement: Let $Q$ and $T$ be types with decidable equality, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $s$ be a natural number such that the binary value of $w$ is $s$. Suppose a configuration $a$ of the specified three-tape machine is in its sweep entry state; within the interval of offsets from $-1$ to $|w|$, tape 0 stores $w$ starting at its head, tape 2 is blank, and tape 1 is blank at every offset from $-1$ to $2s+1$. After encoding the digits as symbols and adjoining the machine's state tag, there is a time $t\le 18(s+|w|)+32$ when the machine reaches its designated exit state, having avoided that state at every earlier time; up to and including time $t$, every work-tape head stays within distance $2s+|w|+3$ of its initial position. At time $t$, all configuration data except the state and work tapes agree with the encoded starting configuration, and tape 1 has been overwritten on the $2s+1$ cells beginning at its initial head position by $s$ blank-cell symbols, one marked cell symbol, and then $s$ blank-cell symbols; tape contents outside that interval are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Initial configuration $a$ has the specified sweep entry state
